samples.summary: New design-doc bullet overstates the behaviour: "A dry run never reaches the network" is now a universal claim, but many read commands still fetch under --dry-run
samples.evidence: The added bullet reads: "Reads honour the flag too: `docs list`, `docs get`, `sheets tabs list`, and `sheets cells get` print their GET without fetching. A dry run never reaches the network, so it burns no rate limit and emits no access log even when the command is harmless." The second sentence is a blanket guarantee, yet in the same tree `notes list` (packages/cli/src/commands/notes.ts:35), `notes get` (:76), `slides list`/`slides get` (packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:35,76), `files list`/`files get` (packages/cli/src/commands/files.ts:85,105), `sheets export` (packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:39) and `api-keys list` (packages/cli/src/commands/api-keys.ts:31) all issue the request regardless of `opts.dryRun`. A design doc that promises an invariant the implementation only partially satisfies is worse than an enumerated list; either scope the sentence to the four commands or cover the rest.
searchedFor: read notes.ts, files.ts, slides.ts, api-keys.ts, sheets-export.ts action bodies

samples.summary: Only 4 of the CLI's read commands were fixed; the equivalent reads in notes/slides/files/sheets-export/api-keys still hit the network under --dry-run, leaving an inconsistent surface
samples.evidence: `docs list`/`docs get` gained a dry-run branch, but the byte-identical sibling commands `notes list`, `notes get`, `slides list`, `slides get`, `files list`, `files get` (all of which call listDocuments/getDocument exactly like docs) were left untouched, as were the read-only `sheets export` and `api-keys list`. §8.2 of docs/design/cli.md describes `--dry-run` as a global flag behaviour, and the agent workflow in §? relies on it being predictable; an agent that learns `docs get --dry-run` is safe will reasonably assume `notes get --dry-run` is too and be wrong. If the originating issue asked for read commands to honour the flag, this is a partial implementation.

samples.summary: The cells dry-run branch re-derives the three-way endpoint choice and the range encoding instead of reusing HttpClient's path builder, so the preview can silently drift from the real request
samples.evidence: Lines 24-29 duplicate both the `range?.includes(':')` dispatch at line 35-39 and the `?range=${encodeURIComponent(range)}` form in HttpClient.getCells (packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:341). The comment even admits the coupling ("encodes the range exactly as `HttpClient.getCells` does"). A shared path-building helper (or having the client expose the resolved URL) would keep one source of truth; as written any change to getCells' query shape must be mirrored here by hand. Existing dry-run branches duplicate simple literal paths, so this is a pattern extension rather than a new sin — hence minor — but this is the first one with real branching logic.

samples.summary: Unrelated scope creep: an unrelated CI lane-selection test fix is bundled into a CLI --dry-run change
samples.evidence: The change to `resolve fail-safes` (adding GITHUB_EVENT_NAME/GITHUB_REF_NAME to the empty-WAFFLEBASE_CHANGED_AREAS case) has nothing to do with `--dry-run` on read commands; it fixes a branch-dependent flake in scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs. It may well be a correct fix, but it belongs in its own change so it can be reviewed and reverted independently of the CLI behaviour.

samples.summary: `docs get`'s dry-run branch sits outside the try/catch while `docs list`'s sits inside, so config-resolution errors take different paths in sibling commands
samples.evidence: docs.ts:125 places `if (opts.dryRun) { printDryRun(getConfig(opts), ...) }` before the `try`, whereas docs.ts:78 (docs list) and cells.ts:143 place it inside. `getConfig` can throw (missing workspace/server), and only in the second form does it surface through `outputError` as the documented JSON error envelope. Purely a consistency preference here since tabs.ts:14 follows the same outside-the-try shape.

finding.summary: New design-doc bullet overstates the behaviour: "A dry run never reaches the network" is now a universal claim, but many read commands still fetch under --dry-run
finding.evidence: The added bullet reads: "Reads honour the flag too: `docs list`, `docs get`, `sheets tabs list`, and `sheets cells get` print their GET without fetching. A dry run never reaches the network, so it burns no rate limit and emits no access log even when the command is harmless." The second sentence is a blanket guarantee, yet in the same tree `notes list` (packages/cli/src/commands/notes.ts:35), `notes get` (:76), `slides list`/`slides get` (packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:35,76), `files list`/`files get` (packages/cli/src/commands/files.ts:85,105), `sheets export` (packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:39) and `api-keys list` (packages/cli/src/commands/api-keys.ts:31) all issue the request regardless of `opts.dryRun`. A design doc that promises an invariant the implementation only partially satisfies is worse than an enumerated list; either scope the sentence to the four commands or cover the rest.
searchedFor: read notes.ts, files.ts, slides.ts, api-keys.ts, sheets-export.ts action bodies

verdict.reason: The quoted bullet exists verbatim at docs/design/cli.md:822-827, including the blanket sentence "A dry run never reaches the network, so it burns no rate limit and emits no access log even when the command is harmless." The enumerated four commands do honour the flag (docs.ts:78 for `docs list`, docs.ts:125 for `docs get`), but the universal claim is contradicted in the same tree: `notes list` (notes.ts:35) and `notes get` (notes.ts:76) call listDocuments()/getDocument() with no opts.dryRun branch; `slides list` (slides.ts:35) and `slides get` (slides.ts:76) likewise, since that file's dryRun guards sit only at lines 60/94/112/141/197/238; `files list` (files.ts:85) and `files get` (files.ts:105) are unguarded while guards exist at 38/58/118/136; `sheets export` (sheets-export.ts:39) contains no dryRun reference at all; `api-keys list` (api-keys.ts:31) likewise (the whole file lacks dryRun handling). No shared middleware short-circuits the HTTP client for these actions — each awaits getClient(opts) directly. A design doc stating an implementation-wide invariant the code only partially satisfies is a design-doc-discipline fit violation in this lens, so the finding is real and blocking; no refutation ground (not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope) applies.

verdict.reason: The absence is factually real (notes/slides/files list|get, sheets export, api-keys list have no dryRun branch and HttpClient does not intercept), so I found no counterexample — but it is not blocking under the design-fit rubric. The originating issue's scope, as recorded in docs/tasks/active/20260816-cli-dry-run-read-commands-todo.md, is exactly four commands: "docs list, docs get, sheets tabs list, sheets cells get", with acceptance criteria stating the envelope must print "for all four commands". All four are implemented (docs.ts:78-81, docs.ts:125-127, tabs.ts:14-15, cells.ts:20-30) and tested (test/read-dry-run.test.ts). The design doc was updated consistently and does NOT promise the behaviour for the siblings: docs/design/cli.md:824-827 enumerates precisely those four commands, contradicting the finding's premise that §8.2 states a blanket global read behaviour. Extending to notes/slides/files list|get would be scope beyond the issue, not a missing acceptance criterion; the residual inconsistency is a pre-existing minor follow-up, not a spec-conformance violation of this change.
